extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and contributors (especially new editors attempting to create or locate an article)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for locating or creating a Wikipedia article when a requested title does not exist; covers searching existing pages, account/autoconfirmation requirements, drafts/wizard, redirects, deletion checks, and related sister projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account and autoconfirmed requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to log in or create an account and be autoconfirmed to create new articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a prerequisite for creating pages; if you are not logged in or not autoconfirmed you must either create an account and meet autoconfirmation requirements or use an alternative submission route (article wizard, draft submission, or request a new article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the article wizard or submit a draft / request new article
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatively, you can use the article wizard to submit a draft for review, or request a new article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot create the article directly (e.g., due to account restrictions or uncertainty about notability/format), follow the article wizard process or submit a draft so experienced editors can review and help integrate it into the encyclopedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search existing articles before creating
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for "Aboriginal jokes" in existing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before creating a new page, search Wikipedia to see if the topic already exists under another title, as a section of another article, or within related pages; this avoids duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for pages that link to the title
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for pages within Wikipedia that link to this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding inbound links can show whether the subject already appears elsewhere (as a redirect or section) and can help you decide whether a standalone article is needed or a redirect/section is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check sister projects for related content
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for 'Aboriginal jokes' on one of Wikipedia's sister projects: Wiktionary, Wikibooks, Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikiversity, Commons, Wikivoyage, Wikinews, Wikidata, Wikispecies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related material might exist on another Wikimedia project better suited to the content (e.g., quotations on Wikiquote, media on Commons), so check those before creating a new Wikipedia article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay or caching may hide recently created pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Other reasons this message may be displayed: If a page was recently created here, it may not be visible yet because of a delay in updating the database; wait a few minutes or try the purge function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you or someone else recently created the page and it doesn't appear, allow time for database updates or use the purge function to refresh the view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization and redirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles on Wikipedia are case sensitive except for the first character; please check alternative capitalizations and consider adding a redirect here to the correct title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify alternative spellings and capitalization variants before creating a new page; if the correct title differs only by capitalization or minor spelling, create a redirect rather than a duplicate article.

rubrics_metrics.name: If page was deleted, consult the deletion log
rubrics_metrics.description: If the page has been deleted, check the deletion log, and see 'Why was the page I created deleted?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previous attempt to create the article was deleted, review the deletion log and guidance on deletion reasons to understand issues (notability, sourcing, policy violations) and address them before attempting recreation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alternative titles or spellings and consider redirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Please search for 'Aboriginal jokes' in existing articles; check alternative capitalizations and consider adding a redirect here to the correct title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes checking alternate titles/spellings and using redirects to avoid duplicate or fragmented coverage; helps ensure readers find the topic even if different terms are used.
